title: Digital Technologies in Geriatric Rehabilitation Care at the Winkelwaldklinik Nordrach: Needs-Based Implementation and Multimodal Evaluation Short title: Needs-Based Digitalization in Rehabilitation Care
summary: The evidence regarding the use of digital technologies in geriatric rehabilitation in Germany has so far been limited and fragmented, particularly within the statutory health insurance system (GKV). National findings also reveal varying degrees of digitalization and a range of implementation barriers. Against the backdrop of rising needs and staffing shortages, a context-specific examination of digital technologies within real-world care structures is necessary. The research project examines how digital technologies can be sustainably implemented in inpatient rehabilitative care (rehab care) based on care needs along real-world care pathways. The research setting is the geriatric care unit at the Winkelwaldklinik Nordrach rehabilitation clinic.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Employees working at the Winkelwald Clinic. This includes registered nurses, specifically those with at least three years of training, whether or not they hold a supervisory role, as well as nursing assistants and care assistants, and other care-supporting professions such as service assistants, hospitality staff, supply assistants, and secretaries. In addition, other occupational groups are included. These include, for example, employees in management, physicians, IT staff, physical therapists, speech therapists, and occupational therapists, as well as custodians and cleaning staff.
A prerequisite for participation is that participants speak and understand German to a degree sufficient for the aforementioned survey formats and are able to provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
The following individuals are excluded: those under the age of 18; those who are not employed by Winkelwaldklinik; employees who do not have sufficient German language skills to participate in the planned survey formats;  and those who are unable or unwilling to provide informed consent.
